record.context_brief: Examples with alpha not equal to plus or minus one
record.original_question: Are there useful examples of invariant dually flat statistical manifolds in which the alpha-connections use alpha not equal to plus or minus one, rather than only the classical alpha = plus or minus one cases?

evidence.quote: Give good examples of the use of α-connections where α is not ±1.
Are there any useful examples of invariant dually flat spaces with α 6= ±1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold equipped with a family of torsion-free affine connections $\{
abla^{(\alpha)}\}_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}$ such that, writing $
abla^{(0)}$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $g$ and $T$ for a totally symmetric $(0,3)$-tensor (the Amari–Chentsov tensor), one has
$$g(
abla^{(\alpha)}_X Y, Z) \;=\; g(
abla^{(0)}_X Y, Z) \;-\; 	frac{\alpha}{2}\, T(X,Y,Z)$$
for all vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on $M$. The connections $
abla^{(\alpha)}$ and $
abla^{(-\alpha)}$ are mutually dual with respect to $g$. The triple $(M,g,
abla^{(\alpha)})$ is called a statistical manifold; it is dually flat (for the parameter $\alpha$) if both $
abla^{(\alpha)}$ and $
abla^{(-\alpha)}$ are flat (zero curvature and torsion). When $M$ is a parametric family of probability distributions, $g$ the Fisher information metric, and $T$ the Amari–Chentsov skewness tensor, the structure is moreover required to be invariant under sufficient statistics (i.e., invariant in the sense of Chentsov).

Question: Exhibit a non-trivial example of an invariant statistical manifold $(M,g,
abla^{(\alpha)})$ that is dually flat for some value $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ with $\alpha
eq \pm 1$, or prove that no such example exists beyond the classical exponential/mixture ($\alpha=\pm 1$) cases.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references on information geometry emphasize the dually flat structure of exponential and mixture families corresponding to $\alpha=\pm 1$. While the family of $\alpha$-connections is well studied for all $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, no widely cited example of a useful invariant dually flat statistical manifold with $\alpha\neq\pm 1$ was located in the search; the question appears to remain an open call for examples rather than a settled result.

status_evidence.title: Canonical Divergence for Flat α-Connections: Classical and Quantum
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses flat α-connections and dually flat structures, with the standard emphasis on α=±1.
status_evidence.claim: Literature on flat α-connections focuses on α=±1; general flat α≠±1 invariant examples are not standard.

status_evidence.title: An Elementary Introduction to Information Geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Survey treating α-connections and dually flat manifolds, highlighting exponential and mixture families.
status_evidence.claim: Useful invariant dually flat examples are typically the e- and m-connections, i.e. α=±1.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of the alpha-connections on the statistical manifold of normal distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes α-connections on normal distributions; curvature does not vanish for α≠±1 in general.
status_evidence.claim: For common parametric families the α-connections fail to be flat outside α=±1.
